answer: Tie each identity to a slow, costly credential that cannot be cloned cheaply. Require every agent to lock a small stake in a shared vault for a cooling period, like water freezing into a glacier: creating thousands of fake identities then demands thousands of separate stakes and waiting periods, while one honest agent pays only once. Reputation from attested work accrues to that staked identity, so abandoning it is expensive. The fable that quantity alone equals influence fails when influence must be earned slowly and lost on proven misbehavior.
